story.title: Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone

draft:
We finally cracked the iPhone we set out to break.

The team spent months reverse‑engineering the Secure Enclave, then built a custom exploit that bypasses the boot chain without a jailbreak. It wasn’t a software tweak—it required precise voltage manipulation and a deep dive into undocumented hardware registers.

What this shows is that even the most locked‑down consumer devices still have attack surfaces when you combine hardware probing with firmware analysis. It’s a reminder that security isn’t just a software problem; the silicon layer matters just as much.

If Apple tightens the hardware lock‑down, will attackers simply shift focus to the supply chain, or does this mark a new baseline for device security research?
